# Implement block: Tilt Swipe Actions (React Native)

You are adding the "Tilt Swipe Actions" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A private-banking ledger on warm laid paper: one engraved ink account card with a brass hairline frame and woven cheque lines, a balance set like a cheque in Bodoni Moda (raised brass dollar sign, ivory cents), and "Latest spending" as a ruled ledger of six transactions in one money style (–$114.00). Swipe a transaction right and keep pulling: the line lifts as a strip of heavier paper and breaks into equal shares, one person per detent (2 to 5), each share with the person's monogram, name and amount; yours turns to ink with a brass monogram, the others stay paper. An ink bar rides over the row above ("$96.60 ÷ 2 3 4 5", the count on a brass disc) and the other rows dim. Let go on two or more and the shares heal into one row reading "–$32.20 of $96.60 · Split with Mai, Leo" with small monograms; the requested people's monograms fly from their shares to an ink toast ("Requested $64.40 · Mai and Leo · $32.20 each") with a brass Undo, the week total rolls down. Undo leaves the row whole: its amount rolls back to –$96.60, "of $96.60" fades, the subtitle cross-fades back to "Dining · Yesterday", the week total rolls back and the toast leaves with its monograms. Let go before the first detent and it springs back. Swipe left for Flag and Delete as flush graphite and oxide tiles; past the middle Delete swallows the strip, and a delete folds the slot with an Undo toast. The name never peeks out as a fragment while the row is open. The FAB sits in the tab bar and opens Income, Expense and Transfer. Every row has Split between 2–5 people, Flag and Delete as accessibility actions.

**Motion.** Pan activates after 12 pt horizontally and fails after 10 pt vertically, so the list still scrolls; a tap only counts when the pan failed (8 pt slop), so a flick never flags or deletes. Right pull: content follows at 0.6× up to 72 pt while it fades (20–56 pt) and the paper strip lifts (0–20 pt); detents at 72/132/192/252 pt with 8 pt hysteresis and rubber 0.35 past the last; each detent sets the target count, the bar re-flows on a spring {300 ms, dampingRatio 0.82} whose overshoot opens the seams (snap) instead of drawing a sliver, seams 6 pt stretching 0.07 pt/pt to 8, the far share trails up to 3 pt {180, 0.9}, the new share's monogram grows from 0.8, shares roll in 180 ms (old gone before new is half in), your share turns to ink in 140 ms, one selection haptic per break; the ink bar extends opaquely from its left end in 160 ms, neighbours dim to 28 % (24–52 pt). Release on 2+: Medium haptic, seams heal {480 ms, 0.86}, shares hand over to one strip, after 160 ms the requested monograms fly row → toast (360 ms sheet curve bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), 60 ms stagger, along the row then down the icon column), toast rises 16 pt in 280 ms (opaque early; the "All transactions" link steps aside first), amount and week total roll 300 ms ease-out bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); toast stays 4 s with a draining brass hairline. Undo: the row stays one row; amount, subtitle and "of" line roll and cross-fade back (300 ms ease-out), the toast and its monograms leave in 140 ms. Release before the first detent: spring back {360, 1} with the finger's velocity. Left swipe: 1:1, rubber 0.35 past 85 % and 0.25 to the right; Flag and Delete tiles share the strip, marks fade in once they fit; open at 78 pt or a −500 pt/s flick to −144 pt {420, 0.8, velocity}, close {360, 1}; past 55 % Delete swallows the strip {220, 0.75} with a Medium haptic; delete slides out with the velocity, slot folds 280 ms; the name fades over the first 36 pt. Autoplay LOOP_MS 10000, starting from a reset rest state 0.8 s after launch: split Little Saigon Kitchen to 3 (0.7–2.9 s), swipe Metro card open (3.7–4.25 s), Undo the request (5.6 s), tap Metro shut (7.1 s), rest; any touch stops it (a half-pulled split springs back), resumes 3.5 s after. Reduce Motion: no follow, trail or scale; the count changes in a 150 ms ease-out, springs become 180 ms timings, numbers and the toast cross-fade, haptics stay.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
